extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants and law firms seeking to file German utility models (Gebrauchsmuster)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for filing a German Utility Model (Gebrauchsmuster), including filing channels, eligibility (PCT national phase), translation and amendment/assignment options, examination regime, timing, and fees. Aimed at applicants (and law firms) using the GlobalIPCo/Prisma IP online system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online filing channel and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: German Utility Models (otherwise known as Gebrauchsmuster) can now be filed online via GlobalIPCo. GlobalIPCo and Prisma IP (a German patent law firm) have created an easy-to-use online system for filing national phase, convention and direct German Utility Models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only national phase German Utility Models are available to general users; direct and convention German Utility Models are available to law firms that register on the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing from a PCT application (national phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: A German Utility Model can easily be filed from a PCT patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GlobalIPCo system supports filing a German Utility Model based on a PCT application (i.e., national phase entry). Note that general users are limited to national phase filings on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To file a German Utility Model, the PCT patent specification must be translated into German.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation of the specification into German is a prerequisite for filing; ensure accurate German translation of the PCT specification before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted amendments and change of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The GlobalIPCo system permits change of applicant (assignment) and amendment of the patent specification upon filing the German Utility Model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may effect assignment and make amendments to the specification at filing via the system — factor these options into filing strategy and required documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights granted and term duration
rubrics_metrics.description: German Utility Models extend the same rights as German patents, albeit for 10 instead of 20 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models provide patent-like rights but for a shorter maximum term (10 years), which may influence choice between patent vs. utility model protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination regime and typical issuance timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas German patents are subject to substantive examination, German Utility Models are only subject to formal examination and certificates are typically issued within 2-3 months of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because there is no substantive examination, utility model protection is faster to obtain; however, lack of substantive examination can affect enforceability/validity risk and may require later opposition or nullity proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and cost structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost: Filing (including receipt of certificate): $570. Response to office action (if any): $200. Postage (optional): $110 per parcel, provided that up to 6 certificates may be included in a parcel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for the base filing fee plus potential office-action responses and optional postage; multiple certificates can be consolidated (up to 6) per parcel to save postage costs.
